1: # UnknownID — Hackathon Implementation Specification
2: 
3: **Version:** 1.0 | **Prepared:** October 20, 2026  
4: **Intended recipient:** Autonomous software-engineering agent / hackathon team  
5: **Target build window:** 48 hours, October 21–22, 2026  
6: **Deliverable:** Working web UI, reproducible experimental-data pipeline, adaptive virtual MS/MS measurement planner, scientifically honest evaluation and exportable investigation reports.
7: 
8: > **Agent mandate:** Implement a narrow, rigorous **closed-world, single-compound LC-ESI-MS/MS identification assistant** that actively requests the next collision energy when an initial spectrum is ambiguous. Use real, independent public experimental spectra for the virtual instrument. Do **not** claim novel structure elucidation, an instrument driver, or general commercial Compound Discoverer parity. Do not fabricate accuracy or dataset sizes. Complete the data audit before committing to the active-identification result.
9: 
10: ## 0. Executive product specification
11: 
12: **User story.** A researcher has an MS/MS spectrum from an unknown small molecule. The program searches a known reference-candidate library, explains why different compounds are plausible, and — if the evidence is insufficient — selects a collision energy for an additional spectrum that is expected to reduce uncertainty. In the hackathon a *virtual mass spectrometer* reveals the corresponding **previously hidden measured spectrum**, rather than an AI-generated spectrum. A separate module handles spectral prediction for *planning* and must never access that hidden observation. The program updates its ranking, either reports an identity with appropriate limitations or abstains, and exports an evidence trail.
13: 
14: **Scientific hypothesis to evaluate:** For a genuinely ambiguous known-library identification subset, an adaptive collision-energy choice can improve identification per additional acquisition compared with fixed-energy and random-energy policies.
15: 
16: **Scope:** small molecules (not peptides, polymers, complex mixtures), positive-ion ESI, singly charged `[M+H]+`, collision-induced dissociation (CID), one verified Bruker maXis Impact LC-QTOF cohort, experimental reference standards. Initially support only fixed collision energies 10/20/30/40/50 eV. No automatic hardware control.
17: 
18: **Novel capability:** budgeted experiment planning in the presence of competing molecular hypotheses, with evidence-backed abstention. Existing library search, spectral interpolation, and MS/MS predictors are *components*, not claimed inventions.
19: 
20: **Success depends on the data audit.** If the selected public cohort does not contain enough nontrivial, precursor-ambiguous identities, report this and switch to the explicitly labeled fallback (§3.8). Do not weaken the mass tolerance merely to create harder identification examples.
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## 1. Verified scientific sources and software dependencies
25: 
26: ### 1.1 Primary dataset — intentionally narrow and homogeneous
27: 
28: **MassBank, University of Athens contributor:**
29: - Repository: https://github.com/MassBank/MassBank-data
30: - Data location: `Athens_Univ/` directory in that repository.
31: - Record specification: https://github.com/MassBank/MassBank-web/blob/dev/Documentation/MassBankRecordFormat.md
32: - Stable public MassBank archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3378723
33: - Example *individual* candidate record: https://massbank.eu/MassBank/RecordDisplay?id=MSBNK-Athens_Univ-AU260701 — Ethion; LC-ESI-QTOF; CID; `[M+H]+`; CE 10 eV; standard compound, CC BY.
34: - Published multi-energy cohort description: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9400100/ and https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jcim.2c00620 — 2022 paper *Augmentation of MS/MS Libraries with Spectral Interpolation for Improved Identification*. This study reports **549 compounds**, measured on a Bruker maXis Impact LC-ESI-QTOF with `[M+H]+`, at **10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 eV**. The authors use a reduced reference library and evaluate held-out energy spectra. **549 is the literature cohort, NOT the guaranteed post-filter count of our current snapshot.**
35: 
36: **Why this source:** It supplies genuine experimental alternatives at a known collision-energy grid with comparatively consistent instrumentation. It is far more defensible for an experiment-selection simulation than arbitrary GNPS/MassBank pooling. The 2022 paper already establishes interpolation is possible; our independent question is **which energy to acquire next**.
37: 
38: ### 1.2 Core code
39: 
40: | Role | Source | How used |
41: |---|---|---|
42: | Source records | https://github.com/MassBank/MassBank-data | Download primary raw .txt records and pin commit |
43: | MassBank format | https://github.com/MassBank/MassBank-web/blob/dev/Documentation/MassBankRecordFormat.md | Parse record and analytical-method metadata correctly |
44: | Spectral parsing, normalization, matching | https://github.com/matchms/matchms and https://matchms.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ | Cosine/modified cosine, MS/MS processing |
45: | Molecular normalization | https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit and https://www.rdkit.org/docs/ | Canonical SMILES, InChIKey, neutral exact mass, chemical validity |
46: | Statistics | https://scipy.org/ and https://scikit-learn.org/stable/ | Interpolation, calibration, bootstrapping, analysis |
47: | Optional MGF parsing | https://pyteomics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/data.html | Read MGF for later user uploads; raw MassBank parser is required first |
48: | UI | https://docs.streamlit.io/ and https://plotly.com/python/ | Interactive dashboard and mirror spectra |
49: | Optional agent coordinator | https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/ | Constrained workflow; state machine is preferable if faster |
50: | Optional spectral prediction stretch | https://3dmolms.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage/msms_prediction.html | Energy-conditioned structure→MS/MS templates on wider candidate pools; separate optional milestone and validate licensing/model support |
51: | Optional harder benchmark | https://github.com/pluskal-lab/MassSpecGym | External retrieval benchmark; **not** substitute for the multi-CE primary dataset |
52: | Optional raw-data processing | https://github.com/mzmine/mzmine | Out-of-scope for first 48 hours; avoid raw mzML import complexity |
53: | Optional broader library | https://library.gnps2.org/libraries | P2 expansion only after harmonizing instrument, provenance and licensing |
54: 
55: **Prior work to acknowledge:** The 2022 JCIM spectral-interpolation study above. Do not claim interpolating across collision energies is novel. MassBank record licenses are **per record** (`LICENSE` metadata may include CC BY, CC BY-SA, NC, etc.); check and attribute each reused record. Do not download or redistribute the proprietary NIST20 library.
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 2. Architecture and trust boundary
60: 
61: ```
62:                       SCIENTIST / STREAMLIT UI
63:                                   |
64:                       spectra + precursor metadata
65:                                   v
66:                   +--------------------------------+
67:                   | CandidateRetriever             |
68:                   | exact adduct/mass + ref spectra|
69:                   +--------------------------------+
70:                                   |
71:                        shortlist + scores
72:                                   v
73:                   +--------------------------------+
74:                   | EvidenceEvaluator              |
75:                   | cosine, diagnostic fragments,  |
76:                   | neutral losses, uncertainty    |
77:                   +--------------------------------+
78:                                   |
79:                   +--------------------------------+
80:                   | Planner                        |
81:                   | simulate possible outcomes at  |
82:                   | each AVAILABLE energy; choose  |
83:                   | expected information gain      |
84:                   +--------------------------------+
85:                                   |
86:                          choose 30 or 40 eV
87:                                   |
88:                          VirtualInstrument
89:                        [SEALED EXPERIMENT ORACLE]
90:                                   |
91:                    measured observation at CE
92:                                   v
93:                   +--------------------------------+
94:                   | PosteriorUpdater + Critic      |
95:                   | reconcile, QC, abstain, report |
96:                   +--------------------------------+
97:                                   |
98:                     rank + evidence + export
99: ```
100: 
101: **Hard isolation rule:** `OracleStore` stores experimental observations at hidden energies. `Planner`, `CandidateRetriever`, `ReferenceStore`, `LLM`, all embeddings, caches and training/calibration processes cannot read the oracle for evaluation compounds. `VirtualInstrument.measure(case_id, energy)` is the **only** endpoint that reveals an observation, and only after an explicit action. Log every call. `ground_truth_identity` is readable by the benchmark scoring process only, never by agent or candidate scoring.
102: 
103: **No deceptive “agent” layers.** Deterministic scientific functions do the numerical work. An LLM may summarize candidate evidence, propose tests through a bounded tool schema, and explain non-identifiability. For v1 the numerical acquisition rule is implemented in Python and may be invoked by the LLM agent. The LLM must not invent peak masses, formula assignments, measured spectra or posterior probabilities.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## 3. DATA SELECTION: implement this first, before writing the UI
108: 
109: ### 3.1 Acquire and freeze a source snapshot
110: 
111: ```bash
112: mkdir -p data/raw
113: # Sparse clone minimizes transfer; preserve commit SHA in dataset manifest.
114: git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/MassBank/MassBank-data.git data/raw/massbank
115: cd data/raw/massbank
116: git sparse-checkout set Athens_Univ
117: git rev-parse HEAD
118: ```
119: 
120: If sparse checkout is unsupported, use the archive or release referenced above and record its DOI/version. Preserve original `.txt` files. In `data/manifest.json`, include source URL, commit SHA/release, retrieval date, processing config version, per-record accession, license, and SHA256 of raw bytes. Never silently refresh the source after evaluation is frozen.
121: 
122: ### 3.2 Parse **raw record fields**, not filename guesses
123: 
124: Required fields (original MassBank tags):
125: 
126: ```
127: ACCESSION
128: LICENSE
129: COMMENT (especially standard/reference confirmation)
130: CH$SMILES
131: CH$LINK: INCHIKEY
132: CH$FORMULA
133: CH$EXACT_MASS
134: AC$INSTRUMENT
135: AC$INSTRUMENT_TYPE
136: AC$MASS_SPECTROMETRY: MS_TYPE
137: AC$MASS_SPECTROMETRY: ION_MODE
138: AC$MASS_SPECTROMETRY: IONIZATION
139: AC$MASS_SPECTROMETRY: FRAGMENTATION_MODE
140: AC$MASS_SPECTROMETRY: COLLISION_ENERGY
141: MS$FOCUSED_ION: PRECURSOR_M/Z
142: MS$FOCUSED_ION: PRECURSOR_TYPE OR ION_TYPE
143: PK$NUM_PEAK
144: PK$PEAK (multiline mz, intensity, relative intensity)
145: ```
146: 
147: Handle escaped/whitespace variants, repeatable `COMMENT`, `CH$NAME`, `CH$LINK` lines, and `PK$PEAK` ending at `//`. Preserve the original collision-energy **string**, parsed numerical value **and unit**. MassBank permits `eV`, volts, normalized percentages and ramps; these **must not** be blindly combined. MassBank record format is the source of truth.
148: 
149: ### 3.3 Inclusion criteria (strict experiment-cohort policy)
150: 
151: Accept a molecule/record only if all relevant conditions are met:
152: 
153: 1. **MS2** data, **LC-ESI-QTOF**, **positive** ionization, **CID**, `[M+H]+`, single-charged. Require the same validated instrument *model* (Bruker maXis Impact) across compared spectra, not just generic QTOF. Exclude GC-APCI and other Athens records even if they share directory/contributor.
154: 2. CE reported as **one fixed numeric value in eV**, exactly one of `{10,20,30,40,50}` within a small parsing tolerance. Exclude missing CE, collision-energy ramps, percent NCE, unspecified volts, and ambiguous units. Do not convert NCE to eV generically.
155: 3. A real standard/reference compound where metadata supports it (e.g., `CONFIDENCE standard compound` / reference-standard designation). Do not treat tentative level-2/propagated annotations as ground truth.
156: 4. Valid RDKit structure and a stable identity key. Prefer full InChIKey (including stereochemistry); preserve 2D connectivity key separately. Do **not** conflate stereoisomers, tautomers, salts and neutral structures automatically. If ambiguous, exclude the record or flag it and remove from primary evaluation.
157: 5. Formula, SMILES-derived neutral monoisotopic mass, and measured `[M+H]+` precursor m/z are mutually consistent within **10 ppm** by default (configurable, recorded, grounded in instrument/QC). Use proton mass for ion correction; not just +1.0 Da. Where data handling of radicals/adducts is unclear, exclude.
158: 6. For primary complete-case evaluation, the exact molecule has a valid experimental spectrum at **all five energies**, with stable adduct/instrument/fragmentation metadata. Keep a separate partial-case table, but don't silently impute a missing oracle energy.
159: 7. Peaks are finite, m/z > 0, intensity nonnegative, precursor m/z > 0; at least **3 nontrivial peaks** at each oracle energy 20/30/40 after a fixed preprocessing rule; endpoints 10/50 may be sparser and must be logged. Do not selectively remove challenging compounds because the identity model fails.
160: 8. Preserve per-record licensing, and release only data/derived artifacts compatible with the license. Even publicly accessible files may have NC or share-alike conditions.
161: 
162: **Replicates:** If multiple records correspond to identical compound+energy+instrument+adduct, identify whether they are independent runs. Do not count replicates as independent compounds; do not let a replica of the same scan straddle oracle and reference. For MVP, select a documented, precommitted representative per condition by acquisition/QC criteria independent of identification outcomes, or construct a robust consensus within a non-overlapping acquisition group.
163: 
164: ### 3.4 Normalization (fixed before testing)
165: 
166: - Keep raw peaks immutable.
167: - Primary processing: remove invalid peaks, optionally remove tiny peaks below **1% base-peak intensity**, normalize vector to base peak=1, and apply the same rule to library, query and oracle spectra. Do not remove a diagnostically useful peak merely because it is near precursor without reporting it.
168: - Use matched fragment tolerance **0.02 Da** as a **starting configuration** for high-resolution QTOF and test sensitivity at 0.01 and 0.05 Da; don't claim universal physical optimality.
169: - Record total/retained peak counts per energy, instrument and identity.
170: - Matchms `CosineGreedy`/`CosineHungarian` for **same precursor/adduct**; `ModifiedCosineGreedy` is optional for analog matching where mass shifts are intended. Report matched-peak count along with similarity. Do **not** call a cosine score a calibrated molecular identity probability.
171: - Add validity checks: duplicate peaks, masses above possible precursor where relevant, implausible adduct/charge assignments, different collision/ionization methods.
172: 
173: ### 3.5 Split data along TWO orthogonal axes
174: 
175: **Axis A — molecular partition (for tuning/generalization):** Split complete cases by **molecular identity**, preferably grouped by Bemis–Murcko scaffold where chemically meaningful. Train/dev/test target 60/20/20 compounds if size permits; if scaffold bins are too imbalanced, document stratification and use identity-level groups instead. Tune interpolation/calibration only on train/dev. Never use **test molecules' hidden-energy spectra** to train acquisition likelihoods or optimize thresholds.
176: 
177: **Axis B — acquisition energy (the virtual laboratory):** For *every* evaluation molecule:
178: 
179: | Availability | Collision energies | Visible to |
180: |---|---|---|
181: | Static candidate reference library | **10, 50 eV only** | Retriever + evidence + planner |
182: | Initial measured query | **20 eV**, revealed at case start | Agent and UI after case starts |
183: | Queryable, hidden measured observations | **30, 40 eV** | Only `VirtualInstrument.measure(30\|40)` after action |
184: | True compound ID | Not an input feature | Benchmark evaluator only |
185: 
186: This deliberate energy separation is necessary because the Athens dataset may supply only one spectrum per molecule per CE; copying the 30-eV reference spectrum into the 30-eV “oracle” would create a false near-perfect identification. Using 10/50-eV reference spectra for all candidate structures is a valid **known-reference-library** scenario. It is not independent blind *de novo* identification. State this clearly.
187: 
188: **Limitation of five energy levels:** There are only **two optional next energy choices** (30 and 40 eV) after the fixed 20-eV initial scan. Therefore the most defensible decision is **choose 30, choose 40, or stop** (possibly both sequentially). Do not claim unconstrained acquisition optimization over dozens of energies.
189: 
190: ### 3.6 Mandatory dataset audit report — stop/go decision
191: 
192: Before training, generate `reports/data_audit.md` plus `data/curated/audit.parquet` with:
193: 
194: - Counts: raw files, valid parsed records, records surviving each exclusion rule, distinct molecules, and exact 5-energy complete cases.
195: - Counts by collision energy, instrument model, adduct, fragmentation method, license and standard-confidence field.
196: - Unique full InChIKeys and 2D connectivity groups, formula groups, precursor m/z distribution, mass-calculation discrepancies and adduct anomalies.
197: - Average/minimum/median fragment peaks per CE, blank/sparse spectra, duplicates and spectrum-matching sanity checks.
198: - **Difficulty analysis:** For each test case, how many **other reference-library molecules** are plausible at the measured precursor m/z within 10 ppm and the same adduct? How many share the molecular formula? How often does a precursor-only baseline already identify the molecule uniquely? How many initially have a close top-2 spectral-ranking margin?
199: - Demonstration eligibility: number of cases with >=2 chemically plausible identities, number with >=3, and number where two candidate spectra predict significantly different outcomes at 30 vs 40 eV.
200: - Sample provenance table with at least 10 real accessions spread across energies (no invented accession IDs) and exact URLs.
201: - License summary and final train/dev/test identities + deterministic split seed.
202: 
203: **Go/no-go gate (proposed minimum, adjustable only before test freeze):** Prefer >=100 complete cases, >=30 scientifically ambiguous 20-eV identification cases, and >=15 cases with nontrivial 30-versus-40 acquisition choices. These are **feasibility targets**, not claims that the data meets them. If much smaller, present the project as proof-of-concept with an explicit limited sample size; do not imply a broadly reliable active-identification result.
204: 
205: **Do not artificially use a 0.5–1 Da mass window with high-resolution QTOF and then describe the resulting problem as realistic.** A deliberately nominal-mass/low-resolution scenario is acceptable only as a distinct, clearly labeled sensitivity experiment, not the primary scientific claim.
206: 
207: ### 3.7 Candidate universe and unknown/closed-world status
208: 
209: - **Closed-world v1:** The true compound exists in the known candidate reference library; candidate identity and molecular reference templates at 10/50 eV are available. The query identity is hidden, not the existence of candidates.
210: - **Retrieval:** filter by exact precursor/adduct plausibility; prefer experimentally supported candidates over hypothetical ones. Rank by 20-eV observation versus an energy-conditioned **interpolated 20-eV template** from 10/50-eV references, plus diagnostic evidence. If no independent reference candidate lies within mass tolerance, mark case as easy/unambiguous and do not include in the *ambiguous-case* primary metric (but report its prevalence in the full-cohort metric).
211: - Use full InChIKey as distinct candidate when stereo evidence can resolve it; **do not claim MS/MS can distinguish enantiomers without appropriate chiral separation**.
212: - **Open-world/abstention test:** Remove a subset of molecules' reference templates entirely from the candidate library, then check that the model flags “none of the above”; it cannot honestly identify them from this limited library.
213: 
214: ### 3.8 Fallbacks if the primary cohort is not sufficiently ambiguous
215: 
216: **Fallback A (scientifically strongest):** Keep the Athens virtual-lab dataset; evaluate *collision-energy-dependent identity verification* rather than open-ended identification. Supply a curated shortlist of **chemically plausible structural hypotheses** generated using independent chemical structure databases or independent spectrum predictions, with exactly stated evidence. Evaluate whether an extra scan rejects an erroneous candidate, not whether an inherently unique precursor magically becomes identifiable. Do not fabricate spectra.
217: 
218: **Fallback B:** Locate a second *separate*, homogeneous, multi-CE experimental cohort in MassBank/GNPS. Repeat ALL metadata checks and never compare absolute CE across dissimilar instrument/fragmentation modalities. State whether cross-instrument generalization is a separate study.
219: 
220: **Fallback C (ambitious extension):** Use an openly licensed energy-conditioned spectral predictor such as 3DMolMS for candidate structures, with measured Athens scans as the oracle. Verify checkpoint training provenance/leakage and energy/instrument covariate support before using it. Treat predicted spectra as fallible; run error analysis. This broadens candidate coverage, but requires more compute and cannot be assumed reliable in 48 hours.
221: 
222: **Decision rule:** Prefer a rigorous limited demo over a misleading large dataset. If no valid multi-energy cohort or sufficient ambiguity survives, document the blocker and ship a functioning spectral-library evidence explorer without making the active-optimization claim.
223: 
224: ---

226: ## 4. Data model and internal API contracts
227: 
228: Use Pydantic models or typed dataclasses, and serialize JSON/Parquet. Example canonical entities:
229: 
230: ```python

233:     molecule_id: str                  # full standardized InChIKey or audited ID
234:     smiles: str

238:     ion_mode: Literal['POSITIVE']

241:     collision_energy_ev: int
242:     mz: list[float]

283: Use different read permissions for `ReferenceStore`, `OracleStore`, and `EvaluatorStore` (truth identity and ground-truth labels). In a hackathon single-process build, make the separation testable via dependency injection and explicit API boundaries; passing a full DataFrame with all 5 CEs into an agent function is forbidden.
284: 
285: **Required backend operations:**
286: 
287: ```
288: POST /cases/start           -> observation at 20eV + candidate list + initial ranking
289: GET  /cases/{id}/ranking    -> current top candidates, scores, evidence
290: POST /cases/{id}/plan       -> allowed energies + cost + recommended energy + IG
291: POST /cases/{id}/measure    -> {energy_ev:30|40} -> authentic previously hidden measured spectrum
292: POST /cases/{id}/stop       -> final decision and limitations
293: GET  /cases/{id}/report     -> downloadable machine-readable evidence record
294: ```
295: 
296: `/plan` MUST NOT reveal test-oracle peaks or truth labels. The API should reject repeated measurement of the same energy, unsupported energy, a consumed budget, and requests for a nonexistent observation.
297: 
298: ---
299: 
300: ## 5. Identification and active-acquisition algorithms
301: 
302: ### 5.1 Precursor filtering and initial ranking
303: 
304: 1. Use measured precursor m/z and known `[M+H]+` ion to restrict candidates to matching precursor m/z within an explicitly specified ppm tolerance. Do not compare ion species with different adducts.
305: 2. For each candidate `c`, construct a **predicted 20-eV** reference template `S_hat(c,20)` using only its **10- and 50-eV reference** spectra. Start with m/z-aware peak alignment + intensity interpolation. Avoid unconstrained exact-mass binning that mistakenly merges separate high-resolution fragments.
306: 3. Compare observed `S_obs(20)` to predicted template with cosine similarity and minimum matched-peak criteria. Add simple explainable evidence (presence/absence of plausible neutral losses, shared fragments). Formula-constrained fragment checks must be algorithmic, not invented by LLM.
307: 4. Convert similarity to a *ranking score*. For a probability-like weight, calibrate a temperature / likelihood model on training+development groups only. Until verified, label normalized scores **relative support**, not `P(true chemical identity)`.
308: 
309: For interpolation use the 2022 paper's method as a baseline/reference (its supplementary code is linked from the DOI/PMC page), but **do not assume it provides scientifically accurate spectra for every molecule and intermediate CE**. Compare against linear interpolation and nearest-energy templates on dev data.
310: 
311: ### 5.2 Information gain (mathematically correct formulation)
312: 
313: Let `C` be the candidate identity (or `NONE_OF_ABOVE`), and let current observations be `D`. Suppose the current estimated candidate weights are `q(c|D)`. For each available next energy `e ∈ {30,40}`:
314: 
315: \[
316: \operatorname{IG}(e)=H[q(C\mid D)]-\mathbb{E}_{Y\sim p(Y\mid D,e)}\left[H[q(C\mid D,Y,e)]\right].
317: \]
318: 
319: The expectation is over **possible future measured spectra Y**, not the hidden actual spectrum. Choose
320: 
321: \[
322: e^*=\arg\max_{e\in E_\mathrm{available}} \frac{\max(0,\widehat{IG}(e))}{\mathrm{cost}(e)}.
323: \]
324: 
325: Use equal measurement cost as the default unless instrument-specific evidence supports differences. Include a **STOP action** if estimated information gain is too small, the shortlist is already sufficiently resolved, or budget is exhausted.
326: 
327: **Implementable Monte Carlo approximation:**
328: 
329: ```python
330: def choose_next_energy(current_weights, candidate_templates, error_model, allowed):
331:     h0 = entropy(current_weights)
332:     values = {}
333:     for e in allowed:
334:         entropies = []
335:         for _ in range(N_MONTE_CARLO):
336:             c = sample_categorical(current_weights)
337:             # Simulate a *hypothetical* spectrum using a template AND
338:             # uncertainty learned only from train/dev molecules.
339:             y = error_model.sample(template=candidate_templates[c][e], energy=e)
340:             updated = update_candidate_weights(
341:                 old=current_weights, hypothetical_spectrum=y,
342:                 energy=e, templates=candidate_templates,
343:                 error_model=error_model)
344:             entropies.append(entropy(updated))
345:         values[e] = (h0 - mean(entropies)) / acquisition_cost(e)
346:     return max(values, key=values.get), values
347: ```
348: 
349: **Critical:** Never sample `y` from the real test oracle before calling `measure`. This would leak the answer.
350: 
351: ### 5.3 Define a probabilistic observation model, not a handwavy IG number
352: 
353: A practical first model:
354: - Project observed and template spectra onto a fixed fragment m/z grid or a sparse matched-peak feature vector, using validated resolution.
355: - Learn interpolation residual distributions **from train identities** at 20/30/40 eV, conditional on energy and ideally precursor mass/peak-density bins.
356: - Sample noisy spectra around the predicted templates with this error model. Ensure nonnegative intensities and realistic peak dropout.
357: - Build the pseudo-likelihood `log L(Y|c,e) = κ_e × cosine(Y, S_hat(c,e)) + peak_count_terms`, or use a fitted low-dimensional Gaussian likelihood. Estimate `κ_e` and noise scales exclusively from train/dev; explicitly track poor fit.
358: - Update `q(c|D,Y,e) ∝ q(c|D) L(Y|c,e)`. Spectra at different energies are correlated: independent likelihood multiplication may overcount information. Calibrate/temper likelihoods based on dev outcomes, and avoid presenting unverified posteriors as calibrated probabilities.
359: - If data are insufficient to fit a credible likelihood, fall back to an **uncertainty/disagreement acquisition heuristic** (which CE maximizes expected pairwise candidate-template separation weighted by current ranks), and **label it a heuristic, not exact information gain**.
360: 
361: ### 5.4 A strong nonprobabilistic fallback acquisition function
362: 
363: If uncertainty calibration fails, use:
364: 
365: \[
366: U(e)=\sum_{i<j} w_i w_j\;d(\widehat S_{i,e},\widehat S_{j,e})\;\times r_e,
367: \]
368: 
369: where `d = 1 - cosine`, weights `w_i` are current candidate support, and `r_e` is a reliability factor derived from held-out interpolation error at that energy (not oracle labels). This encourages an energy where plausible candidates predict different spectra, **discounting poorly modeled energies**. Compare this to random/fixed even if formal IG is unavailable.
370: 
371: ### 5.5 Final identification / abstention
372: 
373: After acquiring at most two additional real spectra, rerank candidates using the same precommitted scoring/calibration. Output `identified` **only if** held-out calibrated selection criteria are satisfied; otherwise `ambiguous`. Include `out_of_library` where no acceptable candidate matches. Always show accession IDs for each observed reference and clearly identify whether evidence is experimental, interpolated, simulated or inferred. Never generate a fabricated measured spectrum.
374: 
375: ---
376: 
377: ## 6. Scientific evaluation: claims the agent may and may not make
378: 
379: ### 6.1 Baselines — all use the exact same candidate universe and initial query
380: 
381: 1. **Precursor-only:** rank from accurate mass/adduct; quantifies easy cases.
382: 2. **Single-scan:** 20-eV observation versus reference-interpolated 20-eV templates, no additional action.
383: 3. **Always-30:** request 30 eV when allowed, otherwise stop.
384: 4. **Always-40:** request 40 eV when allowed.
385: 5. **Random:** choose 30 or 40 at random, repeat over ≥20 seeded trials.
386: 6. **Cheap disagreement:** choose energy maximizing weighted template separation.
387: 7. **UnknownID planner:** information gain when calibrated; otherwise the explicitly labeled reliability-aware acquisition heuristic.
388: 8. **Oracle best action (diagnostic upper bound only):** hindsight maximum accuracy from trying both real observations. **Not a deployable baseline** and excluded from reported planner performance except as a ceiling.
389: 
390: ### 6.2 Primary results
391: 
392: Evaluate separately on **all held-out complete cases** and the **predefined ambiguous subset**. Ambiguous subset membership MUST be determined from initial 20-eV evidence and calibration rules fixed on dev, NOT from whether adaptive planner later succeeds.
393: 
394: | Metric | Definition |
395: |---|---|
396: | Top-1 accuracy@0, @1, @2 | Correct structure after 0/1/2 extra acquisitions |
397: | MRR / Top-3 accuracy | Candidate ranking quality |
398: | Accuracy-vs-number-of-scans curve | Primary cost/benefit story |
399: | Additional acquisitions to reach threshold | Sample efficiency |
400: | Abstention risk/coverage | Error among accepted identifications vs share accepted |
401: | Calibration | Reliability diagram / ECE / Brier only if probability predictions genuinely calibrated |
402: | Information-gain validation | Predictive IG vs observed posterior entropy reduction; avoid using true labels in planning |
403: | Scientific QC rejection rate | Invalid/adduct-confounded cases excluded and their reasons |
404: | Computational runtime | Per case; no invented GPU savings |
405: 
406: Report uncertainty by **molecule-level bootstrap** (not spectrum-level bootstrap) with 95% confidence intervals on *paired differences*. Never represent 5 collision energies for one molecule as five independent test compounds. If multiple outcomes use one source acquisition, preserve grouping.
407: 
408: **Honest limitations:** A gain on a 549-compound homogeneous reference cohort is *not* proof of de novo structure discovery, cross-instrument robustness, improved clinical diagnostics, or automatic control of a real spectrometer. Mass-spec-only structural identification can be ambiguous for stereoisomers and molecules with similar fragmentation.
409: 
410: ### 6.3 Anti-leakage tests (mandatory in CI)
411: 
412: - Unit test: `Planner` cannot call `OracleStore.read` and receives no oracle handles.
413: - Unit test: for a held-out case, replace hidden 30/40-eV measured peaks with randomized arrays *after planning*; the planned action must remain identical.
414: - Verify selected action energy is logged **before** measurement is revealed.
415: - Verify only 10/50-eV spectra are accessed as references for an evaluation compound.
416: - Verify train/dev/test share no molecule IDs, and no test 20/30/40 measured spectra are used in predictive interpolation fitting or likelihood calibration.
417: - No accession/record duplication across folds that silently encodes the same experimental spectrum.
418: - Verify that precursor mass and formula alone do not dominate the reported ambiguous subset.
419: - Never tune hyperparameters or thresholds against test results.
420: 
421: ---
422: 
423: ## 7. Multi-agent behaviors (bounded, demonstrable, useful)
424: 
425: Use a thin workflow with **three roles**, not an uncontrolled swarm:
426: 
427: **Agent A — Chemical Evidence Analyst** (RDKit + matchms): obtain precursor-consistent structures, plot shared/unexplained fragments and neutral losses, flag questionable matches. Tools: `retrieve_candidates`, `compare_spectra`, `inspect_fragments`.
428: 
429: **Agent B — Experimentalist / Planner** (SciPy/NumPy policy): propose measuring 30 eV, 40 eV, or stopping; output evidence-driven expected gain, cost, and constraints. Tools: `available_measurements`, `score_acquisitions`, `measure`. **Only `measure` can invoke the oracle** after checking policy and budget.
430: 
431: **Agent C — Scientific Critic & Reporter**: reject unsupported confidence claims, verify adduct/instrument consistency, ensure no unsupported structure assignment, cite provenance, and export report. Tools: `qc_check`, `report_evidence`, `export_report`.
432: 
433: Require every LLM agent output to parse against a strict schema. Scientific scoring must remain deterministic and independently testable. Do not allow arbitrary LLM Python execution, model-generated fake spectra, or mutation of frozen data.
434:

542: - No homogeneous multi-energy data? Stop the active planner and report the limitation.
543: - Too few ambiguous candidates? Ship case-specific evidence verification or escalate to a documented wider candidate model, not fake difficulty.

569: **User-facing pitch after results exist:**
570: 
571: > UnknownID combines open chemical libraries and MS/MS scoring with an active virtual experiment planner. Instead of committing to a molecular identity from one ambiguous fragmentation spectrum, it chooses between available experimental collision energies and shows whether the additional authentic measurement resolves the uncertainty. We validate improvements against fixed and random energy choices on a homogeneous, publicly documented experimental cohort, with full provenance and explicit abstention.

575: ## 12. Important scientific nuance and novelty boundaries
576: 
577: 1. **Known-library identification is not de novo molecular structure elucidation.** This MVP ranks reference compounds, not arbitrary new unknown chemistry.
578: 2. **A high library similarity is not proof of molecular identity.** Co-elution, stereochemistry, isomers, shared fragmentation and contamination can cause ambiguity. The product needs an abstention option.
579: 3. **A real alternate-energy spectrum is not necessarily an independent replicate.** Here it is a different acquisition condition, and evidence correlation must be considered in scoring/calibration.
580: 4. **The agent cannot ask for measurements not present in the virtual laboratory**; the available actions are fixed and visible.
581: 5. **Information gain requires an observation likelihood model.** Predicted candidate separation by itself is a heuristic and must be labeled accordingly.
582: 6. **Reference endpoints for the test compound are available by construction.** Evaluation tests a *library-supported identification workflow*, not unseen-structure generalization.
583: 7. **Spectral interpolation across CE has prior art.** The research contribution, if verified, is adaptive resource-aware next-measurement selection and robust evidence handling.
584: 8. **MassBank records differ in per-record Creative Commons licenses.** Observe attribution/redistribution conditions; exclude restrictive records if licensing would block planned distribution.
585: 9. **Cohort selection is not proof of generalizability.** Test on a second independently collected and harmonized cohort before making a broad practical claim.
586: 10. **If mass-only identification uniquely determines almost every case, there is no meaningful active experiment to optimize.** The first-day audit may correctly falsify the project hypothesis. Treat that as a scientific finding and pivot transparently.

"""Canonical typed entities shared by the pipeline, API and UI.

These mirror the contracts in section 4 of the specification.  Pydantic is used
so that every artefact written to disk and every API payload is validated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator


Adduct = Literal["[M+H]+"]


class PeakList(BaseModel):
    mz: list[float]
    intensity: list[float]

    @field_validator("intensity")
    @classmethod
    def _nonnegative(cls, value: list[float]) -> list[float]:
        if any(v < 0 for v in value):
            raise ValueError("intensities must be non-negative")
        return value


class SpectrumRecord(BaseModel):
    """One curated experimental spectrum, normalised to base peak = 1."""

    accession: str
    molecule_id: str  # full InChIKey
    smiles: str
    formula: str
    exact_mass: float
    precursor_mz: float
    adduct: str = "[M+H]+"
    ion_mode: Literal["POSITIVE"] = "POSITIVE"
    instrument_model: str
    instrument_type: str
    fragmentation_mode: Literal["CID"] = "CID"
    collision_energy_ev: int
    mz: list[float]
    intensity: list[float]
    license: str
    source_sha256: str
    is_reference_standard: bool
    name: str = ""
    scaffold: str = ""
    retention_time_min: Optional[float] = None
    source_path: str = ""


class PublicCase(BaseModel):
    """What an agent sees at case start (never contains the source accession)."""

    case_id: str
    observed_20ev_spectrum: PeakList
    precursor_mz: float
    adduct: str = "[M+H]+"
    instrument_model: str
    candidate_ids: list[str]
    measurement_budget: int = 1
    available_energies: list[int] = Field(default_factory=lambda: [30, 40])


class PrivateOracleCase(BaseModel):
    """Evaluator-only.  Never serialised into an agent-facing payload."""

    case_id: str
    true_molecule_id: str
    precursor_mz: float
    split: Literal["train", "dev", "test"]
    hidden_accessions: dict[int, str]
    hidden_spectra: dict[int, PeakList]
    reference_accessions: dict[int, str]


class MatchedPeak(BaseModel):
    observed_mz: float
    template_mz: float
    delta_da: float
    observed_intensity: float
    template_intensity: float


class Evidence(BaseModel):
    candidate_id: str
    similarity_by_energy: dict[int, float]
    matched_peaks_by_energy: dict[int, int]
    matched_fragments: list[MatchedPeak] = Field(default_factory=list)
    unexplained_peaks: list[float] = Field(default_factory=list)
    neutral_loss_agreement: Optional[float] = None
    log_score: float = 0.0
    weight: float = 0.0  # relative support, NOT a calibrated identity probability
    name: str = ""
    formula: str = ""
    smiles: str = ""
    exact_mass: float = 0.0
    precursor_ppm: float = 0.0
    reference_accessions: dict[int, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    is_true_identity_visible_to_evaluator: bool = False


class AcquisitionOption(BaseModel):
    energy_ev: int
    predicted_information_gain: float
    separation: float
    reliability: float
    cost: float
    score: float
    method: Literal["monte_carlo_ig", "disagreement_heuristic"]
    note: str = ""


class Action(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["measure", "stop"]
    energy_ev: Optional[int] = None
    predicted_information_gain: Optional[float] = None

    @field_validator("energy_ev")
    @classmethod
    def _allowed_energy(cls, value: Optional[int]) -> Optional[int]:
        if value is not None and value not in (30, 40):
            raise ValueError("v1 only allows the 30 and 40 eV actions")
        return value


class Ranking(BaseModel):
    case_id: str
    observations: list[int]
    evidence: list[Evidence]
    weights_are_calibrated: bool = False
    note: str = "weights are relative support, not calibrated identity probabilities"


class Plan(BaseModel):
    case_id: str
    observed_energies: list[int]
    available_energies: list[int]
    remaining_budget: int
    recommended: Action
    options: list[AcquisitionOption]
    method: Literal["monte_carlo_ig", "disagreement_heuristic"]
    current_entropy: float
    note: str = ""


class Investigation(BaseModel):
    case_id: str
    observations: list[int]
    candidate_evidence: list[Evidence]
    selected_actions: list[Action]
    decision: Literal["identified", "ambiguous", "out_of_library"] = "ambiguous"
    predicted_identity: Optional[str] = None
    confidence: Optional[float] = None
    limitations: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    qc: Optional[dict] = None
    provenance: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)

"""Deterministic spectral processing and matching.

CosineGreedy follows the standard matchms algorithm: all peak pairs inside the
m/z tolerance are greedily consumed in descending product order.  ``matchms``
itself is used by the test-suite as an independent cross-check.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Iterable, Sequence

import numpy as np

PROTON_MASS = 1.007276466621


@dataclass
class ProcessedSpectrum:
    mz: np.ndarray
    intensity: np.ndarray

    @property
    def n_peaks(self) -> int:
        return int(self.mz.size)

    def as_lists(self) -> tuple[list[float], list[float]]:
        return [float(x) for x in self.mz], [float(x) for x in self.intensity]


def preprocess_peaks(
    mz: Sequence[float],
    intensity: Sequence[float],
    *,
    rel_floor: float = 0.01,
    normalize: bool = True,
) -> ProcessedSpectrum:
    """Remove invalid peaks, drop tiny peaks and normalise to base peak = 1.

    The rule is applied identically to reference, query and oracle spectra and
    is frozen before any evaluation.
    """
    mz_arr = np.asarray(mz, dtype=float)
    int_arr = np.asarray(intensity, dtype=float)
    finite = np.isfinite(mz_arr) & np.isfinite(int_arr) & (mz_arr > 0) & (int_arr >= 0)
    mz_arr, int_arr = mz_arr[finite], int_arr[finite]
    if int_arr.size == 0:
        return ProcessedSpectrum(mz_arr, int_arr)
    base = float(int_arr.max())
    if base <= 0:
        return ProcessedSpectrum(np.array([]), np.array([]))
    keep = int_arr >= rel_floor * base
    mz_arr, int_arr = mz_arr[keep], int_arr[keep]
    if normalize and int_arr.size:
        int_arr = int_arr / int_arr.max()
    order = np.argsort(mz_arr)
    return ProcessedSpectrum(mz_arr[order], int_arr[order])


def _greedy_pairs(
    mz1: np.ndarray, i1: np.ndarray, mz2: np.ndarray, i2: np.ndarray, tol: float
) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    if mz1.size == 0 or mz2.size == 0:
        return []
    candidates: list[tuple[float, int, int]] = []
    # Both arrays are sorted; a vectorised difference is fine at these sizes.
    delta = np.abs(mz1[:, None] - mz2[None, :])
    rows, cols = np.where(delta <= tol)
    for row, col in zip(rows.tolist(), cols.tolist()):
        candidates.append((float(i1[row] * i2[col]), row, col))
    candidates.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[0], item[1], item[2]))
    used1: set[int] = set()
    used2: set[int] = set()
    pairs: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
    for _, row, col in candidates:
        if row in used1 or col in used2:
            continue
        used1.add(row)
        used2.add(col)
        pairs.append((row, col))
    return pairs


def cosine_greedy(
    mz1: Sequence[float],
    i1: Sequence[float],
    mz2: Sequence[float],
    i2: Sequence[float],
    tolerance: float = 0.02,
) -> tuple[float, int]:
    """Return ``(cosine, n_matched)`` for two centroided spectra."""
    a_mz, b_mz = np.asarray(mz1, float), np.asarray(mz2, float)
    a_i, b_i = np.asarray(i1, float), np.asarray(i2, float)
    denom = float(np.sqrt(np.sum(a_i**2) * np.sum(b_i**2)))
    if denom == 0:
        return 0.0, 0
    pairs = _greedy_pairs(a_mz, a_i, b_mz, b_i, tolerance)
    if not pairs:
        return 0.0, 0
    numerator = sum(float(a_i[row] * b_i[col]) for row, col in pairs)
    return float(numerator / denom), len(pairs)


def cosine_hungarian(
    mz1: Sequence[float],
    i1: Sequence[float],
    mz2: Sequence[float],
    i2: Sequence[float],
    tolerance: float = 0.02,
) -> tuple[float, int]:
    """Optional optimal assignment variant (small spectra only)."""
    from scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment

    a_mz, b_mz = np.asarray(mz1, float), np.asarray(mz2, float)
    a_i, b_i = np.asarray(i1, float), np.asarray(i2, float)
    denom = float(np.sqrt(np.sum(a_i**2) * np.sum(b_i**2)))
    if denom == 0:
        return 0.0, 0
    if a_i.size == 0 or b_i.size == 0:
        return 0.0, 0
    delta = np.abs(a_mz[:, None] - b_mz[None, :])
    gain = np.outer(a_i, b_i)
    gain = np.where(delta <= tolerance, gain, 0.0)
    rows, cols = linear_sum_assignment(-gain)
    matched = gain[rows, cols] > 0
    return float(gain[rows, cols][matched].sum() / denom), int(matched.sum())


def matched_peaks(
    mz1: Sequence[float],
    i1: Sequence[float],
    mz2: Sequence[float],
    i2: Sequence[float],
    tolerance: float = 0.02,
) -> list[dict[str, float]]:
    a_mz, b_mz = np.asarray(mz1, float), np.asarray(mz2, float)
    a_i, b_i = np.asarray(i1, float), np.asarray(i2, float)
    pairs = _greedy_pairs(a_mz, a_i, b_mz, b_i, tolerance)
    return [
        {
            "observed_mz": float(a_mz[r]),
            "template_mz": float(b_mz[c]),
            "delta_da": float(a_mz[r] - b_mz[c]),
            "observed_intensity": float(a_i[r]),
            "template_intensity": float(b_i[c]),
        }
        for r, c in pairs
    ]


def neutral_losses(
    mz: Sequence[float],
    intensity: Sequence[float],
    precursor_mz: float,
    *,
    max_peaks: int = 60,
) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    """Return plausible neutral losses ``(loss_da, relative_intensity)``.

    Losses below 5 Da are dominated by isotope/rounding artefacts and are not
    treated as diagnostics.
    """
    mz_arr = np.asarray(mz, float)
    i_arr = np.asarray(intensity, float)
    if precursor_mz <= 0:
        return []
    order = np.argsort(-i_arr)[:max_peaks]
    losses = []
    for index in order:
        loss = float(precursor_mz - mz_arr[index])
        if 5.0 <= loss <= precursor_mz - 1.0:
            losses.append((loss, float(i_arr[index])))
    return sorted(losses, key=lambda item: item[0])


def neutral_loss_agreement(
    observed_losses: Sequence[tuple[float, float]],
    template_losses: Sequence[tuple[float, float]],
    tolerance: float = 0.02,
) -> tuple[float, int]:
    """Intensity-weighted Jaccard-style agreement of neutral-loss series."""
    if not observed_losses or not template_losses:
        return 0.0, 0
    used: set[int] = set()
    matched_weight = 0.0
    n_matched = 0
    for loss, intensity in observed_losses:
        best_index, best_delta = None, tolerance
        for index, (tloss, _) in enumerate(template_losses):
            if index in used:
                continue
            delta = abs(loss - tloss)
            if delta <= best_delta:
                best_index, best_delta = index, delta
        if best_index is not None:
            used.add(best_index)
            matched_weight += intensity
            n_matched += 1
    total = sum(i for _, i in observed_losses)
    return (matched_weight / total if total else 0.0), n_matched


def align_spectra(
    mz_a: Sequence[float],
    i_a: Sequence[float],
    mz_b: Sequence[float],
    i_b: Sequence[float],
    tolerance: float = 0.02,
) -> list[tuple[int | None, int | None]]:
    """Greedy one-to-one alignment, returning index pairs with ``None`` gaps."""
    a_mz, b_mz = np.asarray(mz_a, float), np.asarray(mz_b, float)
    a_i, b_i = np.asarray(i_a, float), np.asarray(i_b, float)
    pairs = _greedy_pairs(a_mz, a_i, b_mz, b_i, tolerance)
    used_a = {r for r, _ in pairs}
    used_b = {c for _, c in pairs}
    aligned: list[tuple[int | None, int | None]] = [(r, c) for r, c in pairs]
    aligned += [(r, None) for r in range(a_mz.size) if r not in used_a]
    aligned += [(None, c) for c in range(b_mz.size) if c not in used_b]
    aligned.sort(key=lambda pair: (a_mz[pair[0]] if pair[0] is not None else 1e9))
    return aligned


def spectrum_cosine(
    first: ProcessedSpectrum, second: ProcessedSpectrum, tolerance: float = 0.02
) -> tuple[float, int]:
    return cosine_greedy(first.mz, first.intensity, second.mz, second.intensity, tolerance)


def iter_top_peaks(
    mz: Iterable[float], intensity: Iterable[float], n: int = 10
) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    pairs = sorted(zip(mz, intensity), key=lambda item: -item[1])
    return pairs[:n]

"""Energy-conditioned reference templates.

The static library only ever contains the 10 and 50 eV reference spectra.  All
templates at 20/30/40 eV are interpolations of those two endpoints, so the
planner has no access to the hidden 20/30/40 eV observations by construction.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Iterable, Sequence

import numpy as np

from unknownid.core.spectra import ProcessedSpectrum, align_spectra, preprocess_peaks


@dataclass
class TemplateResult:
    spectrum: ProcessedSpectrum
    method: str
    endpoint_agreement: float  # cosine between the 10 and 50 eV references
    n_peaks_10: int
    n_peaks_50: int


def _weighted_mz(mz_a: float, i_a: float, mz_b: float, i_b: float, t: float) -> float:
    denom = i_a * (1.0 - t) + i_b * t
    if denom <= 0:
        return 0.5 * (mz_a + mz_b)
    return (mz_a * i_a * (1.0 - t) + mz_b * i_b * t) / denom


def interpolate_linear(
    ref_low: ProcessedSpectrum,
    ref_high: ProcessedSpectrum,
    target_ev: float,
    *,
    low_ev: float = 10.0,
    high_ev: float = 50.0,
    tolerance: float = 0.02,
) -> ProcessedSpectrum:
    """First-order interpolation of both m/z and intensity across energy.

    Peaks present at only one endpoint fade in/out linearly.  This is a
    transparent baseline, not a replacement for the published interpolation
    models; the audit/report compare it against nearest-endpoint templates.
    """
    t = (target_ev - low_ev) / (high_ev - low_ev)
    t = min(max(t, 0.0), 1.0)
    aligned = align_spectra(
        ref_low.mz, ref_low.intensity, ref_high.mz, ref_high.intensity, tolerance
    )
    mz_out: list[float] = []
    int_out: list[float] = []
    for low_index, high_index in aligned:
        if low_index is not None and high_index is not None:
            mz_low = float(ref_low.mz[low_index])
            mz_high = float(ref_high.mz[high_index])
            i_low = float(ref_low.intensity[low_index])
            i_high = float(ref_high.intensity[high_index])
            intensity = i_low * (1.0 - t) + i_high * t
            if intensity <= 0:
                continue
            mz_out.append(_weighted_mz(mz_low, i_low, mz_high, i_high, t))
            int_out.append(intensity)
        elif low_index is not None:
            intensity = float(ref_low.intensity[low_index]) * (1.0 - t)
            if intensity > 0:
                mz_out.append(float(ref_low.mz[low_index]))
                int_out.append(intensity)
        else:
            intensity = float(ref_high.intensity[high_index]) * t
            if intensity > 0:
                mz_out.append(float(ref_high.mz[high_index]))
                int_out.append(intensity)
    if not int_out:
        return ProcessedSpectrum(np.array([]), np.array([]))
    mz_arr = np.asarray(mz_out)
    int_arr = np.asarray(int_out)
    order = np.argsort(mz_arr)
    mz_arr, int_arr = mz_arr[order], int_arr[order]
    int_arr = int_arr / int_arr.max()
    return preprocess_peaks(mz_arr, int_arr, rel_floor=0.0, normalize=True)


def nearest_endpoint(
    ref_low: ProcessedSpectrum,
    ref_high: ProcessedSpectrum,
    target_ev: float,
    *,
    low_ev: float = 10.0,
    high_ev: float = 50.0,
) -> ProcessedSpectrum:
    return ref_low if abs(target_ev - low_ev) <= abs(target_ev - high_ev) else ref_high


def build_template(
    ref_low: Sequence[float],
    int_low: Sequence[float],
    ref_high: Sequence[float],
    int_high: Sequence[float],
    target_ev: float,
    *,
    method: str = "linear",
    tolerance: float = 0.02,
) -> TemplateResult:
    low = preprocess_peaks(ref_low, int_low, rel_floor=0.0)
    high = preprocess_peaks(ref_high, int_high, rel_floor=0.0)
    if method == "nearest":
        spectrum = nearest_endpoint(low, high, target_ev)
    else:
        spectrum = interpolate_linear(low, high, target_ev, tolerance=tolerance)
    from unknownid.core.spectra import cosine_greedy

    agreement, _ = cosine_greedy(low.mz, low.intensity, high.mz, high.intensity, tolerance)
    return TemplateResult(
        spectrum=spectrum,
        method=method,
        endpoint_agreement=agreement,
        n_peaks_10=low.n_peaks,
        n_peaks_50=high.n_peaks,
    )


def build_all_templates(
    ref_low: Sequence[float],
    int_low: Sequence[float],
    ref_high: Sequence[float],
    int_high: Sequence[float],
    energies: Iterable[int] = (20, 30, 40),
    *,
    method: str = "linear",
    tolerance: float = 0.02,
) -> dict[int, ProcessedSpectrum]:
    return {
        int(ev): build_template(
            ref_low,
            int_low,
            ref_high,
            int_high,
            ev,
            method=method,
            tolerance=tolerance,
        ).spectrum
        for ev in energies
    }

"""Chemical quality control and curation of raw MassBank records.

Nothing here is inferred from file names.  Every exclusion is recorded with a
stable reason code so the audit can count records surviving each rule.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Iterable

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from rdkit import Chem, RDLogger
from rdkit.Chem import Descriptors, MurckoScaffold, rdMolDescriptors
from rdkit.Chem.inchi import MolToInchiKey

from unknownid.core.spectra import PROTON_MASS, preprocess_peaks
from unknownid.io.massbank_parser import MassBankRecord, iter_record_files, parse_record_file

RDLogger.DisableLog("rdApp.*")

MASSBANK_RECORD_URL = "https://massbank.eu/MassBank/RecordDisplay?id={accession}"


@dataclass
class ChemicalQC:
    ok: bool
    canonical_smiles: str = ""
    formula: str = ""
    exact_mass: float = 0.0
    inchikey: str = ""
    scaffold: str = ""
    ppm_error: float = 0.0
    reasons: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def chemical_qc(record: MassBankRecord, *, ppm_tolerance: float = 10.0) -> ChemicalQC:
    reasons: list[str] = []
    if not record.smiles:
        return ChemicalQC(ok=False, reasons=["missing_smiles"])
    if not record.formula:
        reasons.append("missing_formula")
    if not record.inchikey:
        reasons.append("missing_inchikey")
    if record.precursor_mz is None or record.precursor_mz <= 0:
        return ChemicalQC(ok=False, reasons=reasons + ["invalid_precursor"])

    mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(record.smiles)
    if mol is None:
        return ChemicalQC(ok=False, reasons=reasons + ["rdkit_invalid_smiles"])
    if len(Chem.GetMolFrags(mol)) != 1:
        return ChemicalQC(ok=False, reasons=reasons + ["multi_component_smiles"])
    if Chem.GetFormalCharge(mol) != 0:
        return ChemicalQC(ok=False, reasons=reasons + ["charged_parent"])

    formula = rdMolDescriptors.CalcMolFormula(mol)
    exact_mass = float(Descriptors.ExactMolWt(mol))
    canonical_smiles = Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, isomericSmiles=True)
    inchikey = MolToInchiKey(mol)

    if record.formula and record.formula != formula and formula not in record.formula:
        reasons.append("formula_mismatch")
    if not inchikey:
        reasons.append("inchikey_unavailable")
    elif record.inchikey and inchikey != record.inchikey:
        # Connectivity-only equality is flagged separately: a stereo mismatch is
        # not silently repaired.
        if inchikey.split("-")[0] == record.inchikey.split("-")[0]:
            reasons.append("stereo_inchikey_mismatch")
        else:
            reasons.append("inchikey_mismatch")

    theoretical_precursor = exact_mass + PROTON_MASS
    ppm_error = (record.precursor_mz - theoretical_precursor) / theoretical_precursor * 1e6
    if abs(ppm_error) > ppm_tolerance:
        reasons.append("precursor_mass_inconsistent")

    scaffold = ""
    try:
        scaffold = MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles(mol=mol)
    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        scaffold = ""

    return ChemicalQC(
        ok=not reasons,
        canonical_smiles=canonical_smiles,
        formula=formula,
        exact_mass=exact_mass,
        inchikey=inchikey,
        scaffold=scaffold,
        ppm_error=ppm_error,
        reasons=reasons,
    )


def _metadata_reasons(record: MassBankRecord, cfg: Any) -> list[str]:
    reasons: list[str] = []
    expected = cfg.get_path("instrument", {})
    if record.instrument != expected.get("model"):
        reasons.append("wrong_instrument_model")
    if record.instrument_type != expected.get("type"):
        reasons.append("wrong_instrument_type")
    if record.ms_type.upper() != expected.get("ms_type", "MS2").upper():
        reasons.append("not_ms2")
    if record.ion_mode.upper() != expected.get("ion_mode", "POSITIVE").upper():
        reasons.append("wrong_ion_mode")
    if record.ionization.upper() != expected.get("ionization", "ESI").upper():
        reasons.append("wrong_ionization")
    if record.fragmentation_mode.upper() != expected.get("fragmentation", "CID").upper():
        reasons.append("wrong_fragmentation")
    if record.precursor_type != expected.get("adduct", "[M+H]+"):
        reasons.append("wrong_adduct")
    if cfg.get_path("filters.require_standard", True) and not record.is_standard_compound:
        reasons.append("not_reference_standard")
    if not record.license_is_redistributable:
        reasons.append("license_not_redistributable")
    if not record.collision_energy_is_fixed_ev:
        reasons.append("collision_energy_not_fixed_ev")
    else:
        energies = [int(e) for e in cfg.get_path("energies.all", [])]
        tolerance = float(cfg.get_path("energies.tolerance_ev", 0.5))
        if not any(
            abs(record.collision_energy_value - e) <= tolerance for e in energies
        ):
            reasons.append("collision_energy_outside_grid")
    if record.num_peak_tagged is not None and record.num_peak_tagged != len(record.peaks):
        reasons.append("peak_count_mismatch")
    if len(record.peaks) < 1:
        reasons.append("empty_spectrum")
    return reasons


def _assigned_energy(record: MassBankRecord, cfg: Any) -> int | None:
    if not record.collision_energy_is_fixed_ev:
        return None
    tolerance = float(cfg.get_path("energies.tolerance_ev", 0.5))
    for energy in cfg.get_path("energies.all", []):
        if abs(record.collision_energy_value - energy) <= tolerance:
            return int(energy)
    return None


def record_row(record: MassBankRecord, qc: ChemicalQC, cfg: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    floor = float(cfg.get_path("filters.relative_intensity_floor", 0.01))
    processed = preprocess_peaks(
        [p.mz for p in record.peaks],
        [p.intensity for p in record.peaks],
        rel_floor=floor,
    )
    metadata_reasons = _metadata_reasons(record, cfg)
    reasons = metadata_reasons + qc.reasons
    energy = _assigned_energy(record, cfg)
    return {
        "accession": record.accession,
        "source_path": record.path,
        "source_sha256": record.sha256,
        "license": record.license,
        "name": record.names[0] if record.names else "",
        "smiles_record": record.smiles,
        "smiles": qc.canonical_smiles if qc.ok else record.smiles,
        "formula_record": record.formula,
        "formula": qc.formula if qc.ok else "",
        "exact_mass": qc.exact_mass if qc.ok else np.nan,
        "molecule_id": qc.inchikey if qc.ok else "",
        "scaffold": qc.scaffold,
        "precursor_mz": record.precursor_mz,
        "adduct": record.precursor_type,
        "ion_mode": record.ion_mode,
        "instrument_model": record.instrument,
        "instrument_type": record.instrument_type,
        "fragmentation_mode": record.fragmentation_mode,
        "collision_energy_raw": record.collision_energy_raw,
        "collision_energy_ev": energy,
        "collision_energy_parsed": record.collision_energy_value,
        "collision_energy_unit": record.collision_energy_unit,
        "retention_time_min": record.retention_time_min,
        "is_reference_standard": record.is_standard_compound,
        "num_peaks_raw": len(record.peaks),
        "num_peaks_retained": processed.n_peaks,
        "raw_mz": [float(p.mz) for p in record.peaks],
        "raw_intensity": [float(p.intensity) for p in record.peaks],
        "mz": processed.mz.tolist(),
        "intensity": processed.intensity.tolist(),
        "ppm_error": qc.ppm_error,
        "passed": not reasons,
        "reasons": reasons,
        "record_url": MASSBANK_RECORD_URL.format(accession=record.accession),
    }


def curate_raw(raw_dir: Path, cfg: Any) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict[str, Any]]:
    from unknownid.paths import MANIFEST_JSON, RAW_MASSBANK

    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    manifest_records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    files = list(iter_record_files(raw_dir))
    for path in files:
        record = parse_record_file(path)
        qc = chemical_qc(record, ppm_tolerance=float(cfg.get_path("filters.ppm_precursor", 10.0)))
        rows.append(record_row(record, qc, cfg))
        manifest_records.append(
            {
                "accession": record.accession,
                "path": str(Path(path).relative_to(raw_dir.parent.parent)),
                "license": record.license,
                "sha256": record.sha256,
            }
        )
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)

    commit = ""
    try:
        import subprocess

        commit = subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "-C", str(RAW_MASSBANK), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True
        ).strip()
    except Exception:
        commit = "unknown"
    manifest = {
        "source_repository": cfg.get_path("dataset.source_repo"),
        "source_directory": cfg.get_path("dataset.contributor"),
        "source_commit": commit,
        "persistent_archive": cfg.get_path("dataset.persistent_archive"),
        "retrieved_at_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "record_count": len(files),
        "processing_config_version": cfg.get_path("version"),
        "parser": "unknownid.io.massbank_parser",
        "records": manifest_records,
    }
    MANIFEST_JSON.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    MANIFEST_JSON.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    return df, manifest


def select_representatives(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Choose one acquisition per molecule+energy using an outcome-blind rule.

    Rule (precommitted, independent of identification outcome): highest number
    of retained peaks, then earliest accession.  Replicates never straddle the
    reference/oracle boundary because the same chosen record is used everywhere.
    """
    candidates = df[df["passed"]].copy()
    candidates = candidates.sort_values(
        ["molecule_id", "collision_energy_ev", "num_peaks_retained", "accession"],
        ascending=[True, True, False, True],
    )
    chosen = candidates.drop_duplicates(["molecule_id", "collision_energy_ev"], keep="first")
    chosen = chosen.copy()
    chosen["replicate_count"] = chosen.set_index(["molecule_id", "collision_energy_ev"]).index.map(
        candidates.groupby(["molecule_id", "collision_energy_ev"]).size()
    )
    return chosen.sort_values(["molecule_id", "collision_energy_ev"]).reset_index(drop=True)


def build_case_tables(
    spectra: pd.DataFrame, cfg: Any
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    energies = [int(e) for e in cfg.get_path("energies.all", [])]
    mid_energies = [int(e) for e in cfg.get_path("energies.mid", [20, 30, 40])]
    min_mid = int(cfg.get_path("filters.min_retained_peaks_mid", 3))
    min_endpoint = int(cfg.get_path("filters.min_retained_peaks_endpoint", 1))

    grouped = spectra.groupby("molecule_id")
    rows = []
    partial = []
    for molecule_id, group in grouped:
        by_energy = {
            int(row.collision_energy_ev): row for _, row in group.iterrows()
        }
        present = sorted(by_energy)
        first = group.iloc[0]
        missing = [e for e in energies if e not in by_energy]
        peak_counts = {
            e: int(by_energy[e].num_peaks_retained) if e in by_energy else 0 for e in energies
        }
        reasons: list[str] = []
        if missing:
            reasons.append("missing_energy")
        if any(peak_counts[e] < min_mid for e in mid_energies if e in by_energy):
            reasons.append("too_few_mid_energy_peaks")
        if any(peak_counts[e] < min_endpoint for e in (10, 50) if e in by_energy):
            reasons.append("too_few_endpoint_peaks")
        if len(group) != len(energies):
            reasons.append("unexpected_energy_duplicates")
        row = {
            "molecule_id": molecule_id,
            "smiles": first.smiles,
            "formula": first.formula,
            "exact_mass": first.exact_mass,
            "scaffold": first.scaffold,
            "name": first["name"],
            "precursor_mz": first.precursor_mz,
            "adduct": first.adduct,
            "license": first.license,
            "n_energies": len(present),
            "energies": present,
            "missing_energies": missing,
            "peak_counts": peak_counts,
            "complete": not reasons,
            "reasons": reasons,
            "accessions": {int(e): by_energy[e].accession for e in present},
        }
        if reasons:
            row["partial_reasons"] = reasons
            partial.append(row)
        else:
            rows.append(row)
    complete = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    partial_df = pd.DataFrame(partial)
    return complete, partial_df

"""Explainable candidate evidence: cosine, matched peaks, neutral losses."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace
from typing import Mapping, Sequence

import numpy as np

from unknownid.core.models import Evidence, MatchedPeak
from unknownid.core.posterior import softmax
from unknownid.core.retrieve import Candidate
from unknownid.core.spectra import (
    ProcessedSpectrum,
    cosine_greedy,
    matched_peaks,
    neutral_loss_agreement,
    neutral_losses,
)


class EvidenceEvaluator:
    """Deterministic, independently testable candidate scorer.

    The score is intentionally low-dimensional::

        score(c, e) = kappa_e * cosine(S_obs(e), S_hat(c, e))
                      + w_nl * neutral_loss_agreement
                      - penalty if too few peaks matched

    A softmax of these scores is *relative support*, never a calibrated
    molecular-identity probability.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        tolerance_da: float = 0.02,
        kappa: float = 8.0,
        neutral_loss_weight: float = 0.05,
        unmatched_penalty: float = 0.35,
        min_matched_peaks: int = 2,
        prior_floor: float = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        self.tolerance_da = float(tolerance_da)
        self.kappa = float(kappa)
        self.neutral_loss_weight = float(neutral_loss_weight)
        self.unmatched_penalty = float(unmatched_penalty)
        self.min_matched_peaks = int(min_matched_peaks)
        self.prior_floor = float(prior_floor)

    def explain(
        self,
        observed: ProcessedSpectrum,
        candidate: Candidate,
        template: ProcessedSpectrum,
        energy: int,
        *,
        kappa: float | None = None,
        precursor_mz: float | None = None,
    ) -> Evidence:
        kappa_value = self.kappa if kappa is None else float(kappa)
        cosine, n_matched = cosine_greedy(
            observed.mz, observed.intensity, template.mz, template.intensity, self.tolerance_da
        )
        matches = matched_peaks(
            observed.mz, observed.intensity, template.mz, template.intensity, self.tolerance_da
        )
        matched_mz = [match["observed_mz"] for match in matches]
        unexplained = [
            float(mz)
            for mz in observed.mz
            if not any(abs(mz - other) <= self.tolerance_da for other in matched_mz)
        ]

        precursor = precursor_mz if precursor_mz is not None else candidate.precursor_mz
        observed_losses = neutral_losses(observed.mz, observed.intensity, precursor)
        template_losses = neutral_losses(template.mz, template.intensity, precursor)
        nl_agreement, _ = neutral_loss_agreement(observed_losses, template_losses, self.tolerance_da)

        log_score = kappa_value * cosine + self.neutral_loss_weight * nl_agreement
        if n_matched < self.min_matched_peaks:
            log_score -= self.unmatched_penalty

        return Evidence(
            candidate_id=candidate.molecule_id,
            similarity_by_energy={int(energy): float(cosine)},
            matched_peaks_by_energy={int(energy): int(n_matched)},
            matched_fragments=[MatchedPeak(**match) for match in matches],
            unexplained_peaks=unexplained,
            neutral_loss_agreement=float(nl_agreement),
            log_score=float(log_score),
            weight=0.0,
            name=candidate.name,
            formula=candidate.formula,
            smiles=candidate.smiles,
            exact_mass=candidate.exact_mass,
            precursor_ppm=(
                (candidate.precursor_mz - precursor) / precursor * 1e6 if precursor else 0.0
            ),
            reference_accessions=dict(candidate.reference_accessions),
        )

    def rank(
        self,
        observed: ProcessedSpectrum,
        candidates: Sequence[Candidate],
        templates: Mapping[str, ProcessedSpectrum],
        energy: int,
        *,
        kappa: float | None = None,
        precursor_mz: float | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[list[Evidence], dict[str, float]]:
        evidence = [
            self.explain(
                observed,
                candidate,
                templates[candidate.molecule_id],
                energy,
                kappa=kappa,
                precursor_mz=precursor_mz,
            )
            for candidate in candidates
            if candidate.molecule_id in templates
        ]
        scores = {item.candidate_id: item.log_score for item in evidence}
        weights = softmax(scores, temperature=1.0)
        weights = {key: max(value, self.prior_floor) for key, value in weights.items()}
        total = sum(weights.values()) or 1.0
        weights = {key: value / total for key, value in weights.items()}
        evidence = [
            item.model_copy(update={"weight": weights.get(item.candidate_id, 0.0)})
            for item in evidence
        ]
        evidence.sort(key=lambda item: (-item.weight, item.candidate_id))
        return evidence, weights


def merge_evidence(
    current: Mapping[str, Evidence],
    observed: ProcessedSpectrum,
    candidates: Sequence[Candidate],
    templates: Mapping[str, ProcessedSpectrum],
    energy: int,
    evaluator: EvidenceEvaluator,
    *,
    kappa: float,
    precursor_mz: float,
) -> list[Evidence]:
    """Append one energy's evidence while retaining prior similarities."""
    merged: dict[str, Evidence] = dict(current)
    for candidate in candidates:
        molecule_id = candidate.molecule_id
        if molecule_id not in templates:
            continue
        fresh = evaluator.explain(
            observed,
            candidate,
            templates[molecule_id],
            energy,
            kappa=kappa,
            precursor_mz=precursor_mz,
        )
        previous = merged.get(molecule_id)
        if previous is None:
            merged[molecule_id] = fresh
        else:
            similarity = dict(previous.similarity_by_energy)
            similarity.update(fresh.similarity_by_energy)
            matched = dict(previous.matched_peaks_by_energy)
            matched.update(fresh.matched_peaks_by_energy)
            merged[molecule_id] = previous.model_copy(
                update={
                    "similarity_by_energy": similarity,
                    "matched_peaks_by_energy": matched,
                    "matched_fragments": fresh.matched_fragments,
                    "unexplained_peaks": fresh.unexplained_peaks,
                    "neutral_loss_agreement": fresh.neutral_loss_agreement,
                    "log_score": fresh.log_score,
                }
            )
    return list(merged.values())
